subject: Discrepancy in GCP marketplace payout — ambiguous metered lines
messages:
From: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme-sys.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-14T08:22:00Z
Subject: Payout short by ~€4.2k — lines reference GCP marketplace

Hi Marissa,

We're reconciling April payouts and the merchant remittance from GCP looks short. Our ledger shows three metered-line IDs that were billed to customers (mtr-17891, mtr-17892, mtr-18104) but only the first two appear in the marketplace settlement. The missing line (mtr-18104) maps to a batch of EU customers with VAT-eligible invoices — roughly €4.2k gross.

Can you confirm whether Redwood submitted that line to GCP or if it was merged/rolled into a parent usage ID? I attached our usage extract and the customer-facing invoice. We need this for our tax reclaim and to avoid a short payment to one of our resellers.

Thanks,
Peter Lowe
Head of Billing Operations
Acme Systems

Attachments: acme_usage_bundle_202904.csv (CSV, 3 rows), invoice_202904_acme.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme-sys.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-14T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Payout short by ~€4.2k — lines reference GCP marketplace

Hi Peter — thanks for the detailed packet and the sample invoice. I'm looping in Jonas (marketplace billing) and Neha (tax ops) to triage. Initial notes:

- We see three meter IDs in your CSV; our settlement feed shows two separate settlement lines and one aggregated "batch-legacy" entry on 2029-04-30.
- Aggregation can sometimes collapse legacy micro-lines when customers used an older SKU mapping; that can make traceability hard for VAT pass-through.

Jonas — can you pull the raw ingestion event for mtr-18104 and confirm whether it was consumed into a batch key (batch-legacy-202904) or posted separately? If it merged, we'll need the marketplace invoice mapping table and the timestamp window used for aggregation.

Neha — if this amount is indeed present but rolled into a different settlement line, we need to confirm VAT handling so Acme can claim correctly. If it's missing, we'll escalate to AWS Marketplace with supporting evidence.

Action items: Jonas to confirm ingestion/aggregation; Neha to validate VAT pass-through. I'll coordinate with Acme on evidence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (referencing Peter's originals)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme-sys.com>
Date: 2029-05-15T09:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Payout short by ~€4.2k — lines reference GCP marketplace

Hi all — I pulled the ingestion logs and meter mapping for April. Quick summary:

- mtr-17891 -> mapped to sku:R-WRD-GB-STD -> settlement line SL-4412 (separate)
- mtr-17892 -> mapped to sku:R-WRD-GB-STD -> settlement line SL-4413 (separate)
- mtr-18104 -> mapped to sku:R-WRD-GB-LEGACY -> ingestion timestamp 2029-04-29T23:58:42Z

For April, our upstream batching rule collapsed all R-WRD-GB-LEGACY usage that arrived within 4 hours of midnight UTC into a single aggregated settlement row (batch-legacy-202904) because the legacy SKU uses a separate dimension that the marketplace UI doesn't expose as individual lines. That row was issued on the 30th as SL-4418 with gross €6,200 but it was allocated across three merchant-entities because of a migrated-entity flag. The allocation split table shows only two merchant IDs matched directly to Acme; the third split (~€0.9k) was routed to an historical entity (redwood-legacy-eu) pending reconciliation.

So mtr-18104 is present in SL-4418 but the ledger split routing likely caused Acme's payable to be €4.2k short. I can export the split-by-merchant CSV and the raw ingestion trace if that helps for Acme's accounting and tax reclaim.

Next steps I recommend:
- I will export: split_by_merchant_202904.csv and ingestion_trace_mtr-18104.log
- Marissa: propose we send both to Acme and ask them to confirm the customer-side invoice lines; we'll then submit a formal settlement adjustment request to GCP marketplace support if Acme disputes the allocation.

Jonas
Marketplace Billing Lead
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme-sys.com>
Date: 2029-05-15T12:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Payout short by ~€4.2k — lines reference GCP marketplace

Peter / Marissa — thanks. From a VAT perspective we need two things to allow Acme to recover VAT correctly:

1) A clear mapping that ties the invoice line (customer invoice number) to the marketplace settlement row and a merchant entity ID. The split_by_merchant CSV that Jonas mentioned should include merchant IDs and gross/net/VAT amounts per merchant.
2) Evidence of the marketplace invoice (SL-4418) and any merchant remittance note so Acme can attach to their VAT reclaim. If the split routed part of Acme's revenue to the legacy entity, that is an internal allocation issue and will not create VAT tax liability for Acme, but they need a letter/evidence showing the movement to support reclaim until we fix the mapping.

If Jonas can share the split CSV and ingestion log, I'll draft a short explanation letter for Acme (on Redwood letterhead) that explains the routing and provides the VAT values they need. If we need to push to AWS/GCP for an official settlement adjustment, that will be a separate procurement/finance flow — let me know and I can engage tax counsel.

Neha Kapoor
Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme-sys.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: 2029-05-16T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Payout short by ~€4.2k — lines reference GCP marketplace

Peter — attaching the split file and ingestion trace. See short summary below and requested ask to AWS Marketplace.

Summary for Acme:
- mtr-18104 was ingested and included in settlement SL-4418 (batch-legacy-202904) but split across merchant entity IDs. The portion that should have been remitted to Acme equals €4,205.20 gross (VAT inclusive). The remaining €915.00 gross was routed to redwood-legacy-eu due to an old entity tag still present on the ingestion event.

Requested action (to AWS Marketplace Support):
1) Please confirm SL-4418 breakdown and confirm the merchant-entity splits recorded on the April settlement file. We need the canonical mapping used by the marketplace to route settled amounts to merchant entity IDs.
2) If the canonical mapping shows Acme should have received the €4,205.20, please initiate a settlement adjustment to issue the shortfall to Acme. Otherwise, provide guidance on corrective remittance process.

Attachments included: split_by_merchant_202904.csv, ingestion_trace_mtr-18104.log, (original Acme attachments referenced).

Peter — we can also provide a Redwood letter that documents the internal routing issue so your tax team has supporting evidence while we resolve the short payment. Let me know if you want me to send that letter to you directly.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
